{{Short description|Mathematical analysis theorem}}
In [[mathematical analysis]], '''Tannery's theorem''' gives sufficient conditions for the [[Interchange of limiting operations|interchanging of the limit and infinite summation operations]]. It is named after [[Jules Tannery]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Loya |first1=Paul |title=Amazing and Aesthetic Aspects of Analysis |date=2018 |publisher=Springer |isbn=9781493967957 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Q45aDwAAQBAJ&q=Tannery's%20theorem&pg=PA216 |language=en}}</ref>

== Statement ==

Let <math> S_n = \sum_{k=0}^n a_k(n) </math> and suppose that <math> \lim_{n\to\infty} a_k(n) = b_k </math>. If <math> |a_k(n)| \le M_k </math> and  <math> \sum_{k=0}^\infty M_k < \infty </math>, then  <math> \lim_{n\to\infty} S_n = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} b_k </math>.<ref>{{cite book |last1= |first1= |title=Theory and Applications of Special Functions: A Volume Dedicated to Mizan Rahman |date=2005 |publisher=Springer |isbn=9780387242330 |editor-last=Ismail |editor-first=Mourad E. H. |location=New York |page=448 |editor-last2=Koelink |editor-first2=Erik}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Hofbauer|first=Josef|date=2002|title=A Simple Proof of <math> 1 + 1/2^2 + 1/3^2 + \cdots = \frac{\pi^2}{6} </math> and Related Identities|journal=The American Mathematical Monthly|volume=109|issue=2|pages=196–200|doi=10.2307/2695334|jstor=2695334}}</ref>

== Proofs ==
Tannery's theorem follows directly from Lebesgue's [[dominated convergence theorem]] applied to the [[sequence space]] <math>\ell^1</math>.

An elementary proof can also be given.<ref name=":0" />

== Example ==
Tannery's theorem can be used to prove that the binomial limit and the infinite series [[Characterizations of the exponential function|characterizations of the exponential]] <math> e^x </math> are equivalent. Note that

: <math> \lim_{n\to\infty} \left(1 + \frac{x}{n}\right)^n = \lim_{n\to\infty} \sum_{k=0}^n {n \choose k} \frac{x^k}{n^k}. </math>

Define <math> a_k(n) = {n \choose k} \frac{x^k}{n^k} </math>. We have that <math> |a_k(n)| \leq \frac{|x|^k}{k!} </math> and that <math> \sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{|x|^k}{k!} = e^{|x|} < \infty </math>, so Tannery's theorem can be applied and

: <math> \lim_{n\to\infty} \sum_{k=0}^\infty {n \choose k} \frac{x^k}{n^k}
=\sum_{k=0}^\infty \lim_{n\to\infty} {n \choose k} \frac{x^k}{n^k}
=\sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{x^k}{k!}
= e^x.  </math>
